original_question: Determine whether the pack-fitness framework of form (4.8) can be extended to movement models with other cognitive mechanisms, and how the resulting fitness changes with perceptual kernel choice or perceptual radius.
target_in_paper: Section 4.2.3, Open Problem 45, which asks for a Lewis–Moorcroft-style analysis of optimal movement strategies using the fitness functional (4.8) for other cognitive movement mechanisms, with explicit attention to how pack fitness varies with perceptual kernel and perceptual radius; the paper also notes that model (2.11) is the case where this can be attempted without modifying (4.8). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of Open Problem 45: it identifies the correct fitness framework ((4.8)), the intended extension to other cognitive movement mechanisms, and the two parameter directions singled out by the paper—choice of perceptual kernel and perceptual radius. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
missing_details: The paper asks for a similar analysis of optimal movement strategies, not only whether the framework can be extended in principle. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The surrounding context is specifically Sect. 4.2.3, i.e. movement models with no population dynamics or explicit resources, where earlier fitness/success measures may not directly apply. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The baseline setting behind (4.8) is a two-pack wolf model with pack space-use distributions u and v; the fitness being measured is the fitness of pack u relative to pack v. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

To make the question stand alone, the functional should be written explicitly: r_u = -μ_0 + ln(σψ) - α∫_Ω u(x)v(x) dx + ln(∫_Ω u(x) H(u(x),v(x)) dx), together with the meanings of μ_0, α, σ, ψ, H(u,v), and Ω. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The paper states that this can be done for model (2.11) without modification; if one moves to other movement models without growth dynamics or explicit resources, one must first construct a biologically reasonable analogue of (4.8) for the species/setting under consideration. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

If perceptual kernel or perceptual radius are mentioned in a stand-alone formulation, they should be tied to the paper’s notation: g is the detection/perceptual kernel, R is the perceptual range, and the perception operator is a_g,R(x,t) = ∫_Ω a(y,t) g(x-y) dy. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

If model (2.11) is named, its role should be made explicit: it is the n-population dynamic scent-marking / dynamic cognitive-map system, with ui evolving by diffusion-advection and pi by deposition-decay dynamics. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' quantifier is relevant to this paper’s formulation; the needed hidden assumptions are ecological/modeling ones instead. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The draft leaves the spatial domain and boundary conditions implicit. Open Problem 45 itself does not fix them anew, so a refined question should either inherit them from the chosen underlying movement model or avoid overspecifying them. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
refined_question: For the two-pack Lewis–Moorcroft fitness framework discussed in Sect. 4.2.3, and in particular for the dynamic scent-marking / cognitive-map model (2.11), can one carry out a comparable analysis of optimal movement strategies using the pack-fitness functional r_u = -μ_0 + ln(σψ) - α∫_Ω u(x)v(x) dx + ln(∫_Ω u(x) H(u(x),v(x)) dx), where u and v are the packs’ space-use distributions, μ_0 > 0 is the natural mortality rate, α is the inter-pack aggression coefficient, σ is the prey-to-offspring conversion rate, ψ is the encounter rate, and H(u,v) is the average prey density induced by the space-use patterns u and v; and, within this framework, how does the resulting pack fitness of u change as the cognitive movement mechanism is varied, especially through the choice of perceptual kernel g or perceptual radius R? If one instead studies another cognitive movement model with no growth dynamics or explicit resources, what biologically justified modification of the functional (4.8) is needed before the same optimal-strategy comparison is meaningful? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
justification: This draft is aimed squarely at Open Problem 45, not at a broader neighboring question. The match is exact in substance: Sect. 4.2 first explains that models such as those in Sect. 2.2 may lack population dynamics and explicit resources, so Lewis–Moorcroft’s framework is introduced as a way to measure fitness in that setting; Sect. 4.2.3 then defines the pack-fitness functional (4.8), explains its two-pack ecological ingredients, and immediately asks whether the same optimal-strategy analysis can be performed for other cognitive mechanisms, with dependence on perceptual kernels and perceptual radii. The same paragraph also states the scope condition that model (2.11) needs no modification, whereas other models without growth dynamics or explicit resources require an adapted version of (4.8). The definitions of perceptual kernel g and perceptual radius R come earlier in Sect. 2.1, and model (2.11) is defined in Sect. 2.2. This is therefore the nearest official formulation, and it is narrower and more faithful than the broader comparison problem in Open Problem 46. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
